topic: Regular Expressions, Text Processing, and BPE

questions.question: Which character, when used as the first character inside square brackets ([^A]), changes the meaning of the bracketed expression to negation?
questions.reasoning: The caret (^) when placed as the first character inside square brackets negates the character class.

questions.question: Which sequence of characters matches any non-digit character?
questions.reasoning: \D is the negation of \d and matches any non-digit character.

questions.question: A regular expression uses the Kleene star operator (*). If the previous character appeared 5 times, how many times will the * operator match?
questions.reasoning: The Kleene star (*) matches the preceding element zero or more times, regardless of how many times it already appeared.

questions.question: In the context of Heaps' Law, what does the exponent beta typically fall between?
questions.reasoning: Heaps' Law describes how vocabulary size grows with corpus size, with beta typically between 0.67 and 0.75.

questions.question: Which process reduces inflected words (like cars or ran) to their dictionary headword form (like car or run)?
questions.reasoning: Lemmatization reduces words to their dictionary headword form (lemma), unlike stemming which just removes affixes.

questions.question: In the BPE learning process, after merging the most frequent pair, how is this new merged token used in the next iteration?

options.A: It is assigned a fixed probability.
options.B: It is treated as a single character/symbol for finding new adjacent pairs.
options.C: It is discarded from the vocabulary.
options.D: It is only used for out-of-vocabulary handling.

questions.reasoning: After merging, the new token is treated as a single unit for finding adjacent pairs in subsequent iterations.

questions.question: What defines a morpheme?

options.A: A unit of text defined by whitespace.
options.B: The smallest meaning-bearing unit of a language.
options.C: The total count of running words in a corpus.
options.D: A word that does not stand on its own (a clitic).

questions.reasoning: A morpheme is the smallest meaning-bearing unit in a language.

questions.question: If the test string is "look up a^b now", which segment matches the regex pattern /a^b/?
questions.reasoning: The pattern /a^b/ literally matches the string 'a^b' (^ is not at the start of the pattern, so it's treated as a literal character).

questions.question: In the BPE training steps demonstrated in the course, what purpose does the _ symbol serve?

options.B: It marks a word boundary (end-of-word symbol).

questions.reasoning: The underscore symbol marks word boundaries in BPE tokenization.

questions.question: When a regex pattern ends with \.$, what specific sequence is it designed to match?

options.A: A line ending with any punctuation mark.
options.C: A period that occurs immediately before the end of a line.
options.D: A period that matches any single character.

questions.reasoning: \. matches a literal period and $ anchors to the end of the line.

questions.question: Why does text normalization often include consulting an abbreviation dictionary before sentence segmentation?

options.B: To classify a period (.) correctly as either part of a word (e.g., Dr.) or a sentence boundary.
options.C: To find the lemma of each word.
options.D: To determine if a sequence contains only alphanumeric characters.

questions.reasoning: An abbreviation dictionary helps distinguish between periods that are part of abbreviations versus sentence boundaries.

questions.question: In a regular expression, the pattern \b represents what concept?

options.B: Matching the start or end of a line

questions.reasoning: \b matches a word boundary position between a word character and a non-word character.

questions.question: Which regular expression pattern would successfully match both "bagel" and "bagels"?
questions.reasoning: The pipe operator | creates an OR condition to match either 'bagels' or 'bagel'.

questions.question: What fundamental function does the asterisk character (*) perform in regular expressions?

options.A: Matches the preceding item exactly one time.
options.B: Matches the preceding item zero or more times.
options.C: Matches the preceding item one or more times.
options.D: Represents an OR operation between two items.

questions.reasoning: The asterisk (*) is the Kleene star operator that matches zero or more occurrences.

questions.question: The regex pattern [e^] would match:

options.B: The pattern e^ followed by nothing
options.C: Either the character 'e' or the character '^'
options.D: Only the start of a line containing 'e'

questions.reasoning: Inside square brackets but not as the first character, ^ is treated as a literal character.

questions.question: Which alias for character sets matches any alphanumeric character or underscore?
What is the main objective of the Byte Pair Encoding (BPE) algorithm in tokenization?

options.A: To perform morphological parsing on word stems.
options.C: To reduce the vocabulary size while retaining frequent subwords.
options.D: To ensure every token is exactly one byte long.

questions.reasoning: BPE aims to create a compact vocabulary by iteratively merging the most frequent character pairs.

questions.question: In the BPE training process, after initializing the vocabulary to all unique characters, what step is repeated until k merges are completed?

options.A: Calculating the perplexity of the current vocabulary.
options.B: Choosing the two symbols that are most frequently adjacent and merging them.
options.C: Replacing all infrequent symbols with an <UNK> token.
options.D: Applying a supervised loss function to the token boundaries.

questions.reasoning: BPE iteratively finds and merges the most frequent adjacent character pair.

questions.question: If a test word is encountered that is not explicitly in the learned BPE vocabulary, how is it typically handled?

options.A: It is assigned a probability of zero and discarded.
options.B: It is replaced entirely by the end-of-word symbol (_).
options.C: The word is split into smaller subword tokens available in the vocabulary.
options.D: The BPE learner is run again to incorporate the new word.

questions.reasoning: Unknown words are broken down into known subword tokens from the BPE vocabulary.
